string.text: Rotate the network tiles and connect every square to the central source.
The whole network is connected. Victory has been recorded for this attempt.
Arrows — cursor A / Enter — turn left D / F — right / 180° S / Space — lock
Changing difficulty will reset only the active Net game. Change difficulty?
The active Net game will be lost. Start a new random puzzle?

Rotate the tiles until every cable end joins another cable end, every tile is connected to the central source, and no loop remains. These are ordinary non-wrapping boards: a cable cannot continue through an outside edge. Victory is recorded only when the complete network is correct.

Click an unlocked tile to turn it anticlockwise. The keyboard can also turn the selected tile clockwise or through 180 degrees. An unpowered end node has a large red centre, which turns green after connection to the source. Cyan cables are powered; amber or red segments expose a loop or an invalid connection.

Lock a tile when you believe its orientation is correct. A locked tile cannot be rotated until it is unlocked. Locking is only a working note: it does not prove that the tile is correct and does not change the victory condition.

Arrow keys move the keyboard cursor. A or Enter turns the current tile left, D turns it right, F turns it through 180 degrees, and S or Space locks or unlocks it. Undo is shown only when a move can be undone. Restart restores the same board; New game generates another random board and asks for confirmation while a game is active.

Closing the PDA or leaving the tab keeps the exact board for the current session. Loading a save resets the active board but keeps the selected difficulty. After victory the completed attempt is locked: rotation, locking, Undo, and Restart are hidden, so that board cannot be replayed for another reward. New game creates a fresh random attempt.

F5/F9 and menu loading preserve the exact active game during the current game process. The reward is fixed when an attempt starts and cannot be rerolled by loading. Easy gives no reward. A completed board cannot be replayed; New game creates a new attempt.
